Tamil Nadu is heading into a tightly contested assembly election in 2026 on April 23, with the ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), the opposition All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), and actor Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) shaping what is no longer a straightforward bipolar contest. The state, with 234 assembly seats, has traditionally alternated between the DMK and AIADMK. This time, the entry of TVK has added uncertainty, especially among younger voters. The DMK, led by Chief Minister MK Stalin, is seeking a second consecutive term. It remains aligned with the Congress and Left parties. The AIADMK, which lost power in 2021, is attempting a comeback and is expected to lean on its ties with the BJP, even as alliances remain fluid. TVK, contesting its first full-fledged election. Smaller yet influential players such as Pattali Makkal Katchi (in alliance with AIADMK), Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (in alliance with DMK), and Naam Tamilar Katchi are expected to impact vote shares across regions, even if they are unlikely to dominate the seat tally in the 234-member assembly. #tamilnaduelections #tnelection #tvkvijay #mkstalin #dmkvsaiadmk #tvkvsdmk #cnbctv18 #livenews #tamilnewslive
